summary: Separate-context review of the ADR-0009 runner-status host-tool closure change
logs: 16 findings, 15 survive at least one refuter

findings.title: Runner-status parser is stricter than dpkg and runs over every installed package, so one unrelated runner package can fail every candidate
findings.description: paragraphs() splits a block with Python str.splitlines(). That function also breaks lines on \x0b, \x0c, \x1c-\x1e, U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029, while Debian control lines end only at \n. installed_status() (lines 192-207) parses every paragraph of the runner's full /var/lib/dpkg/status, not just the packages the closure reaches. runner = providers(installed) (line 226) also runs RELATION (line 72) over the Provides field of every installed package. RELATION rejects names that dpkg's own name check accepts, such as names with '_' (deprecated in dpkg but still allowed). So a single runner package anywhere on the image, including a third-party one unrelated to QEMU, fails resolve() for every Windows candidate. A legal Description containing one of those characters raises 'Malformed Debian control paragraph'; an unusual Provides name raises 'Unexpected Debian relation'. That repeats the KI-0189 'every candidate fails' class. The repo's existing Debian parser, ubuntu_gnome_signed_indexes.paragraphs (lines 44-66), reads lines with readline on b'\n' and does not have this problem. I have not verified that the current ubuntu-24.04 image has such a package: no runner dpkg status is available offline. The normalized relation syntax that dpkg writes into the status file and that dpkg-gencontrol writes into Ubuntu debs (name[:arch] [(op ver)], ' | ', ', ') is handled correctly.
findings.evidence: I ran a probe against the module (scratchpad probe.py). installed_status() on a status paragraph whose Description contains '\x0c' raised 'ValueError Malformed Debian control paragraph'. The same happened with U+2028. 'Provides: foo_bar' raised 'ValueError Unexpected Debian relation: foo_bar'. 'Provides: r' raised 'Unexpected Debian relation: r'. Normalized forms parse correctly: 'perl:any', 'libc6 (>= 2.34)', 'foo:native (>= 1)', 'libstdc++6'. Code: line 149 `for line in block.splitlines():`; line 226 `runner = providers(installed)`.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding holds, though it is a latent robustness problem rather than a confirmed failure.

Mechanics. I ran a scratch probe through ubuntu_gnome_prepare.installed_status() and providers() and reproduced every case the reviewer reported:
- A status paragraph whose Description continuation contains \x0c, U+2028 or U+0085 raises "ValueError Malformed Debian control paragraph".
- `Provides: foo_bar`, `Provides: r` and `Provides: Foo` each raise "Unexpected Debian relation".
- The normalized forms parse correctly: `perl:any`, `libc6 (>= 2.34)`, `foo:native (>= 1)` and `libstdc++6`.

Reach. The code does what the finding says:
- installed_status() parses every paragraph of the copied /var/lib/dpkg/status.
- runner_provided() calls providers(installed), which runs RELATION over the Provides field of every installed amd64/all package before the walk starts.
- resolve(..., runner_status=True) calls runner_provided() with no fallback.
- windows11_candidate.main() calls resolve() directly, so any of these ValueErrors fails the whole candidate.
- Nothing scopes the parse to the packages the closure reaches. The runner image version is recorded but not pinned at prepare time, and GitHub updates the image regularly, so a new image could add a package that triggers this. That is the same "every candidate fails" class as KI-0189.

What weakens the finding without refuting it:
- The relation strictness is deliberate. The "malformed" test case pins refusal of `libc6 [amd64]`.
- I believe dpkg lowercases package names when it writes the status file, so the uppercase case is probably unreachable. Debian policy forbids '_' and one-character names, so Ubuntu archive packages should not trigger the name cases. Only third-party debs on the runner (Microsoft, Google, Adoptium and similar) could.
- The reviewer admits that no package on the real ubuntu-24.04 image is known to trigger this. I could not check that offline either.
- The failure fails closed, with a clear error, on the first prepare run of an affected image.

The splitlines() part is still a real parser bug, not a policy choice. Debian control lines end only at LF, and dpkg accepts a Description containing those characters. The other repo parser, ubuntu_gnome_signed_indexes.paragraphs, splits lines only at LF.

I also found that the same over-splitting can misparse rather than fail: a Description containing \x0c followed by "Provides: qemu-system-x86" injected a Provides field into the parsed paragraph. The later apt simulation and dpkg-query version check limit the damage, so this mainly supports the finding that the parser is wrong.

The mechanism reproduces, the stated conditional impact is accurate, and nonblocking is the right severity. It is not refuted.

I could not refute this finding. Every mechanical claim in it checks out, and it is correctly rated nonblocking.

1. Line 149 really is `for line in block.splitlines():` in paragraphs(), and line 226 really is `runner = providers(installed)` in runner_provided(). installed_status() passes the whole decoded runner /var/lib/dpkg/status through paragraphs() before it filters anything. So every paragraph is parsed, including packages in config-files state and third-party packages. providers(installed) then runs relation_groups(), and with it RELATION, over the Provides field of every installed amd64/all package.

2. I reproduced the failures with a probe in my scratchpad (probe/probe.py), run with the repo's .venv under `-I -B`. Each of these raised `ValueError: Malformed Debian control paragraph`:
   - a Description containing `\x0c`
   - a Description containing U+2028
   - a Description containing a lone `\r`
   - an unrelated paragraph in `deinstall ok config-files` state whose Description contains `\x0c`

   These Provides values raised `Unexpected Debian relation`: `foo_bar`, the single-character name `r`, and `Foo`. CRLF line endings parse fine, and so do the normalized forms dpkg writes. `relation_groups("perl:any, libc6 (>= 2.34), foo:native (>= 1), libstdc++6, ab (= 1) | bc")` returns the expected groups.

3. The claims about dpkg are right. dpkg's package-name check allows letters, digits and `-+._`; underscore is deprecated but still accepted, and single-character names are allowed. dpkg's status writer re-serializes relations from lowercased package sets, so uppercase does not occur in practice. Underscore and one-character names can occur. dpkg does not reject Description values containing these control or Unicode separator characters; it ends lines only at `\n`. RELATION (`[a-z0-9][a-z0-9+.-]+`) rejects both underscore names and one-character names.

4. Nothing else handles this. No tolerant path exists for unreached packages. The tests feed only synthetic, clean status files (test_ubuntu_gnome_review_regressions.py lines 330-500). Nothing in the repo or CI has run installed_status() on a real runner status, so no evidence shows the real ubuntu-24.04 image parses cleanly. The comparison to the existing parser holds: ubuntu_gnome_signed_indexes.paragraphs reads lines with readline and strips only `\r\n`.

Limits on the finding:
- As the reviewer says, no real image package that triggers this has been shown. The trigger is latent and needs an unusual (most likely third-party) package on the pinned image.
- The failure is fail-closed: it stops availability, not safety, and the error message is explicit.
- splitlines() also appears in the existing fields(), but that function only reads controls of downloaded closure packages. It does not read the whole runner status, so it does not reduce this concern.

The finding is accurate, reproducible with input that dpkg accepts, and not handled elsewhere: a real robustness defect with a nonblocking rating. That is why refuted is false.

findings.title: Installed HOST_ROOTS (python3, acl) stay tied to the archive, and a root apt cannot reinstall silently drops out of both the lock and the runner-provided record
findings.description: With a populated status, `apt-get -qq --download-only --reinstall install <roots>` treats the roots the runner already has (windows11_candidate.HOST_ROOTS includes acl and python3) in one of three ways. (1) If the candidate equals the installed version and that version is downloadable, apt downloads it. This is the expected path and it works. (2) If the archive's candidate is newer, apt upgrades the root. simulate_host_install then refuses the plan, because PLAN_ADD (ubuntu_gnome_host.py:57) never matches 'Inst python3 [old] (new ...)'. So the archive-ahead-of-image failure that ADR-0009 says it ends still applies to installed roots. (3) The candidate can be the installed version while that version cannot be downloaded. Examples: a superseded noble-updates version that apt keeps as candidate because the newer update is phased and this machine is outside the phase, or a version from a non-Ubuntu origin. apt then only prints 'Reinstallation of X is not possible, it cannot be downloaded.' to its normal output, which -qq (line 303) suppresses, and exits 0. resolve() never checks that every root ended up in `controls` (lines 317-376). runner_provided() starts its walk only from downloaded controls and records nothing for that root. The root and its own Depends chain (for python3: python3.12, libpython3.12-stdlib and the rest, which no other downloaded package depends on) end up in neither `packages` nor `runner_provided_packages`. stage_host's tool_pin would catch a missing acl (setfacl), though with a misleading error. Nothing catches a missing python3, or swtpm-tools. Under the old empty status this could not happen, because every root was necessarily downloaded. A manual reviewer check that all 10 HOST_ROOTS are present would catch it, but the code does not enforce it.
findings.evidence: ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:303 `apt = [*environment, "/usr/bin/apt-get", "-c", str(config), "-qq"]`; :309 `"--reinstall"`; :317 `archives = sorted((root / "archives").glob("*.deb"))`. After this there is no check of roots against controls; the only check is the count at :318. runner_provided seeds `pending = list(controls.values())` (:228). windows11_candidate.py HOST_ROOTS contains "acl" and "python3". The earlier review relied on a manual check: docs/evidence/m03-native-candidates-a03aadf-review/review-workflow-result.json:248 'All 10 HOST_ROOTS are present.' ubuntu_gnome_host.py:57 PLAN_ADD = r"Inst ([^\s\[\]()]+) \(([^\s()]+) [^()]*\)(?: \[\])?" refuses the '[installed]' upgrade form.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute the finding. Its core claims hold, and its nonblocking severity is right. One trigger example is wrong, and the practical impact is narrower than the finding implies.

What I verified:
1. Silent reinstall skip. I read apt 2.8.3 from salsa.debian.org. In apt-private/private-install.cc:1083-1089 (TryToInstall), with APT::Get::ReInstall set, if `Pkg->CurrentVer == 0 || Pkg.CurrentVer().Downloadable() == false`, apt only calls `ioprintf(c1out, "Reinstallation of %s is not possible, it cannot be downloaded.")`. That is not an error. In private-output.cc:66-67, InitOutput redirects c1out to devnull when quiet > 1, and resolve() passes -qq. So apt exits 0 and the root is never downloaded.
2. No completeness check. resolve() (ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:317-376) checks only the archive count. It never checks that every root is in `controls`. runner_provided() seeds its walk from `controls.values()` only. A root that was not downloaded is recorded only if some downloaded package depends on it. No new test asserts that roots are a subset of locked plus runner-provided packages.
3. Only acl and python3 are exposed. The a03aadf campaign plan (docs/evidence/m03-w07-win11-campaign-a03aadf/run41505468952/retained/host-install-plan.json) shows the other 8 roots were newly installed. acl and python3 were the only HOST_ROOTS already on the runner.
4. Installed roots still fail when the archive moves ahead. With a populated status, an explicit `install acl`/`install python3` marks the newer archive candidate for upgrade. closed_install_plan's PLAN_ADD does not match `Inst python3 [old] (new …)`, so the plan is refused. For a python3-defaults update, python3-minimal, libpython3-stdlib and python3-dev would be upgraded too. This fails closed and is not a regression; the old empty status behaved the same way. But it means ADR-0009's tradeoff claim, that (B) "ends the dependency on the archive and the runner image moving in step", does not hold for these two roots. (B) also says a package the image already carries is "used as installed and not downloaded", yet the code reinstalls or upgrades them.

Corrections to the finding:
- The phased-update example is wrong for this apt. In apt 2.8.3, policy.cc ExcludePhased returns false unless APT::Get::Phase-Policy is true (LP #1929082 FIXME). The private config sets nothing for it and loads no runner apt.conf.d parts. depcache PhasingApplied is consulted only on upgrade paths (upgrade.cc) and for the held-back display, not for an explicit install. A phased newer python3 or acl therefore becomes the candidate and goes through the fail-closed upgrade path, not the silent one.
- The "non-Ubuntu origin" example does not apply to acl or python3 on this image. The a03aadf review recorded 90 "already the newest version" lines, so both installed versions were downloadable from the archive. GetCandidateVer only picks a non-downloadable installed version when no archive version is newer or equal. The remaining silent trigger is rare: the image's version withdrawn from noble-updates or noble-security with nothing newer published.
- Impact is limited. A missing acl still fails closed at stage_host's tool_pin for /usr/bin/setfacl, though with a misleading error. A missing python3 goes unrecorded, but the campaign already runs on the runner's python3 (`python3 -B scripts/windows11/windows11_vm.py`). ADR-0009 says the runner image is already trusted for Python, and the image version is pinned. The independent lock review checks "All 10 HOST_ROOTS are present" (a03aadf review-workflow-result.json:248).

Net: the absence of a code-enforced roots-completeness check is real, and so is the gap in the archive-ahead claim for installed roots. Both are nonblocking hardening points, not unsafe behaviour, so I am not refuting the finding.

I could not refute the finding's central claim. It is a real but narrow gap, and nonblocking is the right severity. One of its two example triggers is wrong.

What I confirmed:
1. resolve() never checks roots against what was downloaded. In ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py, `roots` is used in only two places: the apt-get argv and the recorded "roots" key. Nothing compares the roots with `controls` or with runner_provided_packages. runner_provided() seeds its walk with `pending = list(controls.values())`, so a root that apt did not download is recorded only if some downloaded package happens to depend on it.
2. apt really does skip such a root silently. I read apt 2.8.2's apt-private/private-install.cc (TryToInstall::operator(), lines 1083-1093). When the candidate equals the installed version and `Pkg.CurrentVer().Downloadable() == false`, apt only prints "Reinstallation of %s is not possible, it cannot be downloaded." to c1out and sets no _error. In private-output.cc (lines 66-67), a quiet level above 1, which `-qq` gives, sends c1out to /dev/null. So the download step exits 0 and prints nothing.
3. A missing acl fails closed, but with an odd error. tool_pin(extracted, "/usr/bin/setfacl") would hit resolve(strict=True) and raise FileNotFoundError. python3 has no tool pin. The reviewed 10f247b lock shows python3=3.12.3-0ubuntu2.1, plus python3-minimal, python3.12 and libpython3.12-stdlib, all present only because of the python3 root. If python3 dropped out, that whole chain would be missing from both `packages` and `runner_provided_packages`. Nothing in install_tools, stage_host or the tests would notice. No test covers a root that apt did not download.
4. Case (2) is real. If an installed root has a newer, normal archive version, `--reinstall install` upgrades it. PLAN_ADD does not match the 'Inst X [old] (new …)' line, so the plan is refused. This fails closed and is not a regression: the old empty-status design refused it too. But it does contradict ADR-0009's (B) wording, "A package the pinned runner image already carries … is used as installed and not downloaded", and its claim that (B) "ends the dependency on the archive and the runner image moving in step". For installed roots, that dependency remains.

Where the finding is wrong:
- The phased-update example does not hold on noble's apt 2.8.x. In apt-pkg/policy.cc ExcludePhased, phasing is ignored unless APT::Get::Phase-Policy is set ("legacy implementation until LP: #1929082"), and the private apt.conf does not set it. PhasingApplied is used only in upgrade.cc and in the kept-back display, not in TryToInstall. So an explicit install of a root whose update is still phasing in gets the newer version as its candidate. That is case (2), which fails closed, not case (3).
- Case (3) therefore needs a rarer trigger: an installed root version that is in none of the noble, noble-updates or noble-security indexes while no newer archive version exists. Examples are a pulled or regressed SRU, or a third-party, backports or proposed origin. Today the runner's acl and python3 come from those archive pockets at identical versions.
- "or swtpm-tools" does not apply. swtpm-tools is not on the runner image; the a03aadf review lists it as newly installed, so it is always downloaded.
- The practical impact of a missing python3 is small. ADR-0009 already says the campaign trusts the runner image's Python, and the lock pins the runner image version.

Net: the defect is real. The code does not enforce that every root lands either in the hashed lock or in the recorded runner-provided set, and under `-qq` apt can drop a root silently. It is narrower than described, because the phasing trigger is wrong. Case (2) is a fail-closed limitation against the ADR's stated goal, not a security hole.

findings.title: dpkg_status_sha256 and the copied status the walk used are discarded, so a reviewer cannot audit runner_provided_packages
findings.description: resolve(runner_status=True) adds dpkg_status_sha256 only to lock.json inside its destination. On the Windows path that destination is work/host-candidate, and the status copy sits in work/apt. stage_host stages only packages, runner_provided_packages and signed_index_chain into host-tools-lock.json. The whole work tree is rmtree'd before retain(). So the status that runner_provided() walked, and even its hash, never reach the reviewed bundle or any retained proof. A reviewer approving the v2 lock by SHA cannot check whether the over-approximated runner-provided list is complete for that status, and cannot spot an omission like the one in finding 2. The dpkg_status_sha256 field is computed but never used.
findings.evidence: windows11_candidate.py:245 `work = args.output / "private-work"`; :319 `host = work / "host-candidate"`; :322 `lock = resolve(owner, work / "apt", host, HOST_ROOTS, runner_status=True)`; stage_host writes only schema/review_state/runner_image_version/tools/packages/runner_provided_packages/signed_index_chain; :405 `shutil.rmtree(work)` runs before :413 `retain(args.output, inputs=True)`. ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:392 `result["dpkg_status_sha256"] = sha(root / "status", DPKG_STATUS_CAP)` is written only to destination/lock.json (:396).

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute this finding. Every factual claim checks out against the working tree, and the gap is real, though it is nonblocking.

1. `dpkg_status_sha256` reaches only a file that is deleted. `ubuntu_gnome_prepare.resolve()` adds `result["dpkg_status_sha256"]` only when `runner_status` is true (`ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:391-394`) and writes it only to `destination/lock.json`. The only caller with `runner_status=True` is `windows11_candidate.py:322`. There the destination is `host = work / "host-candidate"` and the status copy is `work/apt/status`, where `work = args.output / "private-work"`. The GNOME guest path never sets the field; its test asserts `"dpkg_status_sha256" not in result`.
2. The staged lock leaves the hash out. `stage_host` (`windows11_candidate.py:192-220`) writes `host-tools-lock.json` with only `schema`, `review_state`, `runner_image_version`, `tools`, `packages`, `runner_provided_packages` and `signed_index_chain`. Neither the status hash nor the status file is copied into `inputs/`. The new test `test_windows_candidate_host_lock_records_runner_provided_packages` checks exactly that key set and nothing about the status.
3. Nothing from the work tree is retained. `main()`'s `finally` block runs `shutil.rmtree(work)` before `retain(args.output, inputs=True)`. `retain()` in `windows11_inputs.py:441` also skips any path whose first part is `private-work`. So the copied status, its SHA and `host-candidate/lock.json` reach neither the reviewed bundle nor the retained proof. The earlier a5ec1e3 review noted the same pattern for the apt.conf: it is not retained because the work dir is rmtree'd.
4. What does survive is not enough to check that the list is complete. `Owner.command` writes stdout to `args.output/command-NNN.*`, so the live `dpkg-query` output is retained. It only covers the names already in `runner_provided_packages`, so it confirms each row's version but cannot show that a package was left out. Walking the runner packages' own dependencies needs their control data, which lives in the discarded status. The retained signed Packages indexes list only each pocket's newest version. Runner versions that are behind the archive, such as libpcre2-8-0 10.42-4ubuntu2.1 against 2.2 in the archive, are exactly the KI-0189 case, and their control data is not in those indexes.
5. Partial mitigations exist but do not remove the gap. ADR-0009 names the pinned runner image version as the trust anchor, and `install_tools` checks `runner_image_version` and re-checks the recorded rows before and after install. The ADR wording is "records it by name, version and dpkg status". It does not explicitly require keeping the status file, so this is not an ADR violation and not a safety hole. Still, the hash is computed and unit-tested and then never used or kept on the one path that produces it, and an omission from the list cannot be audited from the evidence. That is a real nonblocking provenance and auditability gap, as the finding says.

I could not refute the finding. Its facts all match the code and the workflow. I checked read-only and edited nothing.

1. **The hash only reaches a private file.** `resolve(..., runner_status=True)` in scripts/linux_gnome/ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py sets `result["dpkg_status_sha256"] = sha(root / "status", ...)` and writes it only to `destination/lock.json`. Its only caller with runner_status=True is scripts/windows11/windows11_candidate.py main(), where `host = work / "host-candidate"`, `work = args.output / "private-work"`, and the status copy lands in `work/apt/status`.

2. **Staging drops it.** `stage_host()` writes host-tools-lock.json with only schema, review_state, runner_image_version, tools, packages, runner_provided_packages and signed_index_chain. Neither `dpkg_status_sha256` nor the status file is staged. The new test `test_windows_candidate_host_lock_records_runner_provided_packages` asserts only those keys.

3. **Nothing retained keeps it.** main()'s finally block runs `shutil.rmtree(work)` before `retain(args.output, inputs=True)`, and retain() skips `private-work` anyway. The prepare workflow uploads only `.../retained/` and `retention-failure.json`. Earlier review evidence (a5ec1e3 review) confirms that every member of the Windows candidate ZIP is under `retained/` and that there is no host-candidate/, unlike GNOME.

4. **No other route covers it.** I found no other path that keeps the runner status. The retained command records hold:
   - the downloaded debs' `dpkg-deb -f` control fields;
   - the dpkg-query output for exactly the recorded names, which only mirrors the rows;
   - the apt-get commands, which run with -qq.

   A reviewer can therefore check first-level dependencies of the downloaded debs by name. They cannot check Provides or transitive dependencies of runner packages, so they cannot confirm that runner_provided_packages is complete. On the only runner_status=True path, `dpkg_status_sha256` is dead data.

**Mitigations, which lower the impact but do not remove the gap:**
- ADR-0009 binds runner-provided libraries "only through the reviewed runner image version and the recorded dpkg versions". It does not require the status or its hash to be retained.
- At campaign time, the local-only apt (empty sources) and the simulate-first install still turn any unmet dependency into a failure, and still refuse any plan that replaces or removes a runner package.
- The Windows host-candidate/lock.json was never retained before this change either: empty_status_resolution, roots and package_bytes were dropped too.
- Retaining only the hash would not make the list auditable; the status file itself, or the control fields of the runner-provided packages, would have to be kept.

**Why the finding still stands:** this change computes an integrity field that nothing ever uses. It also moves part of the closure from replayable hashed debs to a runner-derived list whose input is thrown away, which removes the replayability that the earlier design and reviews relied on. Nonblocking is the right severity.

findings.title: Post-install runner re-check has no refusing test; a no-compare mutant survives all new campaign tests
findings.description: The second require_runner_packages call (after the real `apt-get --no-remove install`) is the only guard against the install itself changing or removing a runner-provided package. For example, a downloaded package that Replaces every file of a runner package makes dpkg mark that package as gone. No test makes the runner table differ between the pre-install and post-install queries. RunnerOwner.runner is fixed per instance (test_windows11_host_runtime.py:264). The refusal text "Runner-provided host packages changed during install" appears nowhere under scripts/tests. The ordering test only checks that a second dpkg-query happens after apt, not that its result is compared. ADR-0009's test impact requires tests that refuse a runner whose installed version differs, and only the pre-install path has one.
findings.evidence: `git grep -n "changed during install"` matches only scripts/windows11/windows11_vm.py:391. I wrote a scratch mutant (outside the repo) that replaces only the post-install call with `runner_packages(owner, sorted(reviewed))` and no comparison. I ran the four new campaign tests against it: `.venv/bin/python -I -B -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --rootdir <scratch>/mut <scratch>/mut/test_post_install_mutant.py` gave `11 passed in 0.19s`. The mutant survives.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute the finding. I reproduced it.

1. The refusal text is never asserted. `grep -rn "changed during install"` matches only scripts/windows11/windows11_vm.py:391. Only scripts/tests/test_windows11_host_runtime.py exercises install_tools, runner_packages or require_runner_packages.

2. No test changes the runner table between the two queries. RunnerOwner stores a fixed `self.runner` dict (test line 264) and answers every dpkg-query from it. Nothing changes it during the apt calls. So in every test the pre-install and post-install queries return the same rows.
   - The drift test, `test_windows_runner_provided_drift_fails_before_any_apt` (newer/removed/foreign-only), refuses before any apt call. It covers only the pre-install path.
   - The ordering test, `test_windows_runner_provided_packages_are_checked_before_and_after_install`, checks only that a second Status-Abbrev dpkg-query runs after the second apt-get call. It never checks that the result is compared.

3. I built my own mutant under the scratchpad (/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tanishkalwad-jobapplyv2/17ee071f-b2d5-4e6f-a57e-209b35ae06c1/scratchpad/mut1). It is a copy of scripts/windows11 and scripts/linux_gnome plus the test file. In the copy I replaced the post-install `require_runner_packages(owner, reviewed, "...changed during install")` with `if reviewed: runner_packages(owner, sorted(reviewed))`, which queries but does not compare.
   - Running the whole test file against the mutant gave 73 passed and 1 failed. The failure is unrelated: the scratch copy has no .github/workflows file.
   - Narrowing to the install and runner tests gave 15 passed, 0 failed. That includes all three ordering-test variants, the three pre-install drift variants, the four row-validation variants, the v1-refusal test and the candidate lock test.
   - So the mutant survives.

4. The gap is real, even if small. ADR-0009's test impact asks for tests of "the campaign-time re-check, refusing a runner whose installed version differs". Only the pre-install half of that re-check has a refusing test.
   - The post-install check is the only guard against the real `apt-get --no-remove install` changing a runner-provided package outside the simulated plan. One way that happens is dpkg making a package disappear after a Replaces takeover of all its files.
   - A regression that drops the comparison would go unnoticed.

The production code itself looks correct; the defect is missing coverage, as the reviewer said. That fits the reviewer's "nonblocking" severity.

I could not refute this finding. It reproduces as reported.

1. Code. In /Users/tanishkalwad/jobapplyv2/scripts/windows11/windows11_vm.py, install_tools calls require_runner_packages twice. The first call runs before simulate_install, with "differ from the reviewed lock". The second runs after the real `apt-get --no-remove install` and the locked-package dpkg-query, with "Runner-provided host packages changed during install" (line 391). The second call is the only guard against the real install changing a runner-provided package, for example through Replaces/Conflicts that the --no-remove simulation does not catch.

2. Tests. `git grep -n "changed during install"` matches only windows11_vm.py:391. No test matches that refusal text. RunnerOwner (test_windows11_host_runtime.py:259-291) answers every dpkg-query from one fixed `self.runner` table set in __init__, and no test changes it between the two queries. findings.title: The lock does not record each runner-provided package's dpkg status, and the campaign does not re-check it, though accepted ADR-0009 says it does
findings.description: Accepted ADR-0009 option (B) (docs/DECISIONS.md:469) says: "The lock records it by name, version and dpkg status, and the campaign re-checks those values before any install." For example, a package that was 'hold ok installed' at prepare and is 'install ok installed' at the campaign, or the reverse, passes. The other reading of 'dpkg status' (the status file's digest) is not met either: dpkg_status_sha256 is computed but never reaches the reviewed lock (see the next finding). So a trust-boundary change does not match the text the owner accepted. Neither ADR-0009 nor KI-0189 records that architecture replaced status. Fix: record each package's dpkg Status in its row (and in installed_rows) and require an exact match at the campaign. Otherwise, record the deviation truthfully as an amendment the owner acknowledges.

verdicts.reasoning:

The campaign accepts either "ii " or "hi " and does not compare that against anything recorded at prepare. ADR-0009 (docs/DECISIONS.md:469) does say "name, version and dpkg status".

The conclusion that this is a blocking trust-boundary mismatch does not hold. The dpkg status is recorded by construction and re-checked at both ends.

1. **The status is recorded.** A package can enter runner_provided_packages only if both checks hold:
   - the copied status says "install|hold ok installed" for amd64/all (installed_status in ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py);
   - live dpkg-query reports "ii " or "hi " (installed_rows).

   So every row asserts that the package's dpkg state is "installed" with flag "ok". There is exactly one admissible status, so an explicit field would always hold the same value.

2. **The campaign re-checks that status before any install, and again after it.**
   - runner_packages() refuses any state other than "ii "/"hi ". This covers rc, iU, iF and the reinstreq flag. It also refuses a missing package or a foreign-architecture-only instance.
   - require_runner_packages runs before the simulated install and after the real install.
   - These focused tests passed when run here (12 passed): test_windows_runner_provided_drift_fails_before_any_apt[removed] (state "rc " refused with no apt call), [newer] and [foreign-only], and the before/after ordering assertions.
   - The prepare-side test_runner_provided_refuses_an_unproven_runner_closure[live-unpacked] refuses "iU ".

3. **What the finding treats as a status change is a selection change.** dpkg's Status triple is selection state (install/hold/deinstall/purge), flag (ok/reinstreq) and package state (not-installed … installed). The only thing left uncompared is the selection state, hold versus install.
   - It does not change which files are on disk, so it does not change which libraries QEMU loads.
   - It has no effect at campaign time. The campaign already refuses any simulated plan that replaces or removes a runner package, installs with --no-remove, and re-checks exact versions after the install.
   - The tests accept this on purpose: the [held] case at the campaign, and a live "hi " against a copied "install" at prepare.

4. **The ADR's trust boundary is implemented as written.** The ADR states the binding in its Tradeoffs and Security sections: runner-provided libraries are "bound only through the reviewed runner image version and the recorded dpkg versions". The implementation does exactly that:
   - it pins the image version;
   - it requires an exact name→(version, architecture) match;
   - it requires the installed state, refusing anything else.

   Its Test-impact line asks for refusing "a runner whose installed version differs", and that is implemented and tested. Architecture is an extra binding. It does not replace status, contrary to the finding.

5. **"Blocking" is not supported.** The finding gives no case where the missing explicit field lets different bytes, a non-installed package or a changed version through. Its example, a hold/install flip, is a selection change with no security effect.

At most, the ADR could say "installed dpkg state" instead of "dpkg status". That is a wording clarification, not a defect in the change. Whether dpkg_status_sha256 ever reaches the lock is a separate finding and does not decide this one.

findings.title: A root that apt does not re-download is recorded neither as locked nor as runner-provided
findings.description: ADR-0009 (B) says a package the runner image already carries and that is used as installed is recorded in the lock. The runner_provided() walk starts only from the downloaded control paragraphs (`pending = list(controls.values())`). resolve() never checks that every root is among the downloaded packages. Under the old empty-status resolution every root was necessarily downloaded. Under runner_status=True, roots are downloaded only because of `--reinstall`. When a root's installed version cannot be downloaded from the three private pockets (for example, it came from another origin), apt prints 'Reinstallation of X is not possible, it cannot be downloaded', treats X as already newest and exits 0. That root and its dependency subtree then end up in neither `packages` nor `runner_provided_packages`. The tool pins in stage_host() fail closed for roots that carry a pinned tool (qemu-system-x86, qemu-utils, ovmf, swtpm, xorriso, mtools, wimtools, acl). They do not cover python3 or swtpm-tools, which are both in HOST_ROOTS and have no pinned tool. Fix: in runner-status mode, refuse unless every root is in `controls`, or start the walk from the roots too and record them.
findings.evidence: ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:228 `pending = list(controls.values())`. ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py:305-316 runs apt-get --download-only --reinstall ... install *roots. The roots appear only at :313 (passed to apt) and :387 ("roots": list(roots)); no check compares them with `controls`. windows11_candidate.py:40-51 HOST_ROOTS includes "swtpm-tools" and "python3"; TOOLS/FIRMWARE (:52-64) pin no file from either.

verdicts.reasoning:
I could not refute the finding. The code reads as the finding says, and a scratch probe reproduced the gap.

1. Code path. In runner-status mode, resolve() (scripts/linux_gnome/ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py) passes the roots only to `apt-get --download-only --reinstall ... install *roots` and records them as `"roots": list(roots)`. Nothing compares the roots with `controls`, which holds the downloaded packages. runner_provided() starts its walk from `pending = list(controls.values())` and adds only installed packages reached through Pre-Depends/Depends of downloaded packages. If a root was not downloaded and no downloaded package depends on it, it is in neither `packages` nor `runner_provided_packages`.

2. Reproduced. I wrote a scratch test outside the repo: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-tanishkalwad-jobapplyv2/17ee071f-b2d5-4e6f-a57e-209b35ae06c1/scratchpad/rootprobe/test_root_probe.py. 3. Apt behaviour. This part rests on my knowledge of apt's source, not on a test. In apt's TryToInstall, when the candidate is the installed version and APT::Get::ReInstall is set, a non-downloadable CurrentVer only gets an ioprintf to c1out: "Reinstallation of X is not possible, it cannot be downloaded." That is not an error, and -qq silences c1out, so apt-get exits 0. The installed version is non-downloadable when it is absent from the three private pockets (noble, noble-updates, noble-security) and no newer candidate wins. That can happen if:
   - it came from another origin, or from backports, which the runner's sources have and the private config omits; or
   - a newer noble-updates SRU is being phased and this machine is out of phase. Ubuntu phases SRUs, and phasing applies once the runner status makes the root an installed package.
   Under the old empty-status resolution nothing was installed, so every root was necessarily downloaded.

4. No other check catches it.
   - stage_host's tool_pin extracts only the downloaded debs, so roots with a pinned tool fail closed: qemu-system-x86, qemu-utils, ovmf, swtpm, xorriso, mtools, wimtools and acl.

   - windows11_vm.install_tools re-checks only `runner_provided_packages` and the locked debs.
   - The host-tools-lock.json staged for review does not carry `roots`, so a reviewer comparing the lock would not see the omission either.
   - The new tests assume roots are always reinstalled (the comment says "a reinstalled root"). None covers a root that apt does not download.

5. ADR conformance. ADR-0009 (B) says a package the runner already carries "is used as installed and not downloaded. The lock records it by name, version and dpkg status, and the campaign re-checks those values." An undownloaded root is used as installed but is not recorded, so the change departs from the accepted ADR.

Why it stays nonblocking:
   - The only realistic affected roots lack a tool pin: python3, and swtpm-tools if it were preinstalled.
   - The campaign already runs on the runner's python3, which ADR-0009 already trusts.
   - swtpm-tools' binaries are not used by windows11_vm.py, and the GitHub image probably does not carry swtpm-tools, so it would normally be a fresh download.

The finding is accurate, and the suggested fix is cheap: in runner-status mode, refuse unless every root is in `controls`, or seed the walk with the roots and record them.

I could not refute this finding. The mechanism holds against the code. The ADR text supports calling it a conformance gap, and nonblocking is the right severity.

What I checked in the code:

2. The roots are used only as apt arguments and as `"roots": list(roots)` in the lock. No code compares the roots with `controls` or `rows`.
3. runner_provided() starts its walk from `pending = list(controls.values())` only. A root that was not downloaded is recorded only if a downloaded package depends on it.

5. Owner.command fails only on a nonzero exit. It does not inspect stdout, and apt runs with -qq.
6. simulate_host_install / closed_install_plan see only the downloaded archives.
7. In windows11_vm.install_tools, the campaign checks only the locked packages, the reviewed runner-provided rows, and the tool pins.

The apt behavior, from my recollection of apt's source, not run here: in apt-private/private-install.cc, TryToInstall handles an installed package that MarkInstall does not change and that has APT::Get::ReInstall set, but whose CurrentVer is not Downloadable(). It prints "Reinstallation of %s is not possible, it cannot be downloaded." only as information and carries on, so the run exits 0. I could not run apt on this macOS host, which has no Linux or container tooling.

A realistic trigger beyond "another origin": the private config does not override /etc/machine-id or the preference files, and the env has no SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, so Ubuntu phased updates apply. Suppose a newer phased version of python3 (or acl) is in noble-updates and the runner falls outside the phase. apt pins the phased version to priority 1, so the candidate stays at the installed version. That installed version has been superseded in the noble-updates index and so cannot be downloaded. apt then skips the root silently, and it ends up in neither `packages` nor `runner_provided_packages`.

ADR-0009 (B) says a runner-carried package that is "used as installed and not downloaded" is recorded by name and version. Under the old empty-status resolution every root was always downloaded, so this gap is new.

critic.description: runner_provided() treats a relation group as satisfied when a downloaded package meets it, either by name or by a downloaded package's Provides (prepare.py:225 `downloaded = providers(controls)`, :233 `satisfied = any(name in downloaded ...)`). No new test has a group that only the downloaded closure satisfies. In DOWNLOADED_CONTROLS every group (libc6, awk, foo|bar, libpcre2-8-0, libfdt1, and zlib1g through Pre-Depends) is also met by a runner package. libfdt1 is both downloaded and installed. The resolve fixture's only relation is libc6, which the runner provides. The 'unsatisfied' case meets neither side. On a real runner the opposite is the common case: qemu-system-x86 depends on qemu-system-common, qemu-system-data and seabios, which only the lock provides. A regression on this path would make every Windows candidate fail closed with 'satisfied by neither the lock nor the runner', and only a hosted prepare would catch it. This is a separate gap from the listed 'every alternative' finding: the downloaded half of the lock-or-runner rule, including downloaded Provides, is never exercised. The ADR-0009 test-impact line promises tests for the runner-status resolution.
critic.evidence: I copied scripts/ to the scratchpad and applied two mutants to the copy of ubuntu_gnome_prepare.py, then ran `pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider` on test_ubuntu_gnome_review_regressions.py and test_windows11_host_runtime.py. (1) `satisfied = any(name in downloaded for name in group)` replaced by `satisfied = False`: 99 passed. The one failure was test_the_lifecycle_job_timeout_covers_the_campaign_authority, with FileNotFoundError because .github was not copied, so it is unrelated. (2) `downloaded = providers(controls)` replaced by `{name: [name] for name in controls}`, which ignores downloaded Provides: 26/26 passed in test_ubuntu_gnome_review_regressions.py. Neither mutant is killed.

critic.title: The ADR registry table still omits ADR-0009, though the change marks it ACCEPTED
critic.description: docs/DECISIONS.md keeps a canonical 'Architecture decision records' index table (ID | Title | Status | Date | Spec sections affected). It lists ADR-0001 through ADR-0008 and ends at line 80. The diff changes ADR-0009's section to 'Status: ACCEPTED' and 'decided 2026-11-04' but adds no row for it. The file's own rule says that after approval 'the decision status [is] updated in one coherent change'. A reader of the registry table cannot see that the trust-boundary change for the host-tool lock was accepted. validate_status.py does not check this table, so it passes.
critic.evidence: `grep -n 'ADR-000[0-9]' docs/DECISIONS.md` shows table rows only for ADR-0001..ADR-0008 (lines 73-80). ADR-0009 appears only as the section heading at line 462 and in its body. The diff touches lines 464-465 and 477-479, not the table.

critic.title: ADR-0009 makes the runner image version its trust anchor, but a null version passes on both sides
critic.description: Under ADR-0009 the runtime libraries QEMU loads from the runner are bound only 'through the reviewed runner image version and the recorded dpkg versions'. The ADR says the lock 'already pins' that version. The candidate writes `os.environ.get("ImageVersion")` into the lock (windows11_candidate.py:214), which is None when the variable is unset. The campaign checks `lock["runner_image_version"] != os.environ.get(RUNNER_IMAGE_VERSION)` (windows11_vm.py:335-337). If ImageVersion is absent at both prepare and campaign, null equals null and the image pin is vacuous. Nothing requires a non-empty string. The comparison predates this change, but the change now relies on it as the anchor for every runner-provided package that is not hashed.
critic.evidence: windows11_candidate.py:214 `"runner_image_version": os.environ.get(RUNNER_IMAGE_VERSION)`; windows11_vm.py:335-337 compares it to `os.environ.get(RUNNER_IMAGE_VERSION)` with no isinstance or non-empty check. require_host() checks only RUNNER_ENVIRONMENT/GITHUB_ACTIONS/OS, not ImageVersion. DECISIONS.md ADR-0009: 'whose exact version the lock already pins'.

critic.title: The 'v1 lock without runner-provided rows' test actually sends a lock that has the rows
critic.description: test_windows_v1_host_lock_without_runner_provided_rows_is_refused calls windows_install(..., {"schema": "japp-win11-host-tools-v1"}). windows_install builds the lock as `{"schema": v2, "tools": {}, "runner_provided_packages": [], **lock}` (line ~312-316), so the 'v1' lock still has `runner_provided_packages: []`. The test only checks that a v2-shaped lock relabelled v1 is refused. A real v1 lock, the kind the old candidate produced, has no such key and is never built. A v2 lock that lacks the key, which fails through a bare KeyError in reviewed_runner_packages, is not tested either.
